LONG: the token held is underwater when its mark value is below debt plus the maintenance buffer at `principal` (PerpEngine.sol:1126) - note collateral does not appear, because a long's collateral was already spent into the position. SHORT: underwater when the mark cost of buying back the owed size plus the buffer exceeds `backing` (PerpEngine.sol:1131), where backing is collateral plus the proceeds held at `backing` (PerpEngine.sol:1129).

FIRST, a cached-quote divergence: if `quote` (PerpEngine.sol:1307) no longer equals the registry's quote for the current generation, the engine declares itself dead without consulting the hook at all - this is what makes the book force-closeable after a live rotation. SECOND, the hook's own pool-death flag, read through a try/catch at `isDead` (PerpEngine.sol:1308) that reports NOT dead on any revert, so an unwired or reverting hook fails OPEN for trading and CLOSED for force-closing. Note the registry calls here are NOT wrapped, so a reverting registry bricks both openings and force-closes. DERIVED.

Called at `_checkNotional` (PerpEngine.sol:797) and `_checkNotional` (PerpEngine.sol:826). If depth reads 0 the product is 0 and every non-zero notional reverts. DERIVED.

Its swap semantics are what the sweep cursor at `_openIds` (PerpEngine.sol:950) and the drain loop at `_openIds` (PerpEngine.sol:1009) both depend on.

Quote-to-token at SPOT, the inverse of `_quoteAt` (PerpEngine.sol:709). Used twice in the short open - to size the borrow at `_ethToToken` (PerpEngine.sol:827) and to convert depth into token units for the open-interest cap at `_ethToToken` (PerpEngine.sol:834). Unlike the liquidation path this deliberately uses spot, so borrow sizing follows execution price. The conversion uses two `mulDiv` (PerpEngine.sol:1344) steps against the spot sqrt price.

reachability: Splits every routed fee. With a vault wired, the LP slice and the insurance slice are carved FIRST and stay inside the engine as counters - `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1361) for long-attributed fees, the segregated `tokYieldEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1363) plus its monotonic marker `tokYieldCumulative` (PerpEngine.sol:1364) for short-attributed ones, and `insuranceEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1366) for both. Only the remainder leaves the contract, split by `divShareBps` (PerpEngine.sol:1370) between dividend and treasury and pushed through the non-reverting `_payOut` (PerpEngine.sol:1372). Both recipients are owner-settable at `dividend` (PerpEngine.sol:1724), and a zero address silently forfeits that leg at `dividend` (PerpEngine.sol:1372). DERIVED.

A one-line alias kept for its callers' readability; it is the REVERTING push, so a vault withdrawal or an insurance skim to a recipient that rejects the transfer fails the whole call rather than crediting an IOU. Reached from `_sendEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1643), `_sendEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1649) and `_sendEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1790).

value: sends native to `to` (line 1392); ERC20 transfer of the quote to `to` (line 1401)
reachability: The NON-reverting push, used for every recipient an attacker can choose: the trader, the keeper, the dividend and the treasury. On failure it credits `payoutOwed` (PerpEngine.sol:1405) instead of reverting, which is what keeps one hostile trader from making `forceCloseAllDead` (PerpEngine.sol:998) unsatisfiable. The ERC20 branch decodes the return so a false-returning or blacklisting token also falls through to the credit at `ok` (PerpEngine.sol:1403).
observations: comment at `budget` (PerpEngine.sol:1387) says the forwarded gas is bounded so a recipient cannot consume the settlement budget; only the native branch bounds it at `gas` (PerpEngine.sol:1392), while the ERC20 branch forwards all remaining gas at `call` (PerpEngine.sol:1400).

authority: anyone (pays only the caller's own credit)
value: sends the quote to the caller through `_pushQuote` (line 1414)
reachability: The recovery path for anything `_payOut` (PerpEngine.sol:1388) could not push. Effects precede the interaction - the balance is zeroed at `payoutOwed` (PerpEngine.sol:1413) before the push - and the function carries `nonReentrant` (PerpEngine.sol:1410) but NOT the nesting guard. Note the credit is a bare number: it is booked in whatever quote was live at settlement and paid in whatever `_pushQuote` (PerpEngine.sol:1414) names at claim time. DERIVED.

LONG bad debt. By the time it runs, `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1147) has already been credited with only the reduced repayment, so this ADDS insurance cover back into `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1421), saturating at the buffer balance. Any gap beyond the buffer is simply left as a lower PLV, i.e. socialised to ETH-side stakers.

SHORT bad debt, the mirror case: the buy-back at `_buyExactOut` (PerpEngine.sol:1159) has already spent real balance that was never booked, so this DECREASES the counters - insurance first at `fromIns` (PerpEngine.sol:1429), then `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1432) saturating at zero so an extreme gap cannot underflow and brick the liquidation.

Builds the on-chain snapshot minted with the badge. Entry price is principal over size at `entry` (PerpEngine.sol:1469) and liquidation price is the triggering mark over the same size at `mark` (PerpEngine.sol:1470), both scaled by 1e18 and clamped into uint128 at `liqPrice` (PerpEngine.sol:1481); collateral and bounty clamp into uint96 at `collateralWei` (PerpEngine.sol:1475). Clamping means an out-of-range value misreports rather than reverting the liquidation.

Hybrid trophy delivery, with three guards so a liquidation can never revert on it: a gas floor at `gasleft` (PerpEngine.sol:1492), a code-length check at `col` (PerpEngine.sol:1494) - without which a low-level call to an empty address would report success and silently drop the badge - and a bounded forward at `fwd` (PerpEngine.sol:1496). It tries the stats-bearing selector first at `mintLiquidatorWithStats` (PerpEngine.sol:1499) and falls back to the plain one at `mintLiquidator` (PerpEngine.sol:1509) if the first fails and gas remains. Anything else credits `badgesOwed` (PerpEngine.sol:1515). The collection address comes live from the hook and is therefore not pinned. DERIVED.

authority: anyone (burns only the caller's own credit)
reachability: Claims the IOU form of the badge. It reverts rather than burning the credit when no collection is wired at `col` (PerpEngine.sol:1530), decrements `badgesOwed` (PerpEngine.sol:1531) before the mint loop, and bounds work by the caller-supplied n, which is clamped down to the owed count at `owed` (PerpEngine.sol:1525). The loop makes n TYPED external calls to a hook-chosen collection at `mintLiquidator` (PerpEngine.sol:1534), so a reverting collection reverts the whole claim and the credit survives. DERIVED.

The checked ERC20 send: it accepts an empty return or a decoded true and otherwise reverts at `BadParam` (PerpEngine.sol:1538). Used for the ERC20-quote branch of `_safeTransfer` (PerpEngine.sol:219) and for paying token inventory out at `_safeTransfer` (PerpEngine.sol:1661). Unlike `_payOut` (PerpEngine.sol:1388) it has no credit fallback, so a blacklisting quote token makes the vault-withdraw path revert.

Owner-only, share-less donation into the ETH-side PLV: it raises `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1552) with no shares minted anywhere, so the value is permanently non-withdrawable by the donor and simply lifts the vault's share price. Community capital is meant to arrive through `deposit` (PerpVault.sol:187) instead.

value: ERC20 `transferFrom` of the generation token from the owner (line 1559)
reachability: Token-side twin of the ETH donation. The pull uses the registry's LIVE `currentToken` (PerpEngine.sol:1559) rather than the engine's armed `syncedToken` (PerpEngine.sol:1264), and the return value is NOT checked here - unlike `_pull` (PerpVault.sol:226) and `_safeTransfer` (PerpEngine.sol:1536) - so a token that returns false instead of reverting would credit `plvToken` (PerpEngine.sol:1560) without moving anything. DERIVED. The pull is a direct `transferFrom` (PerpEngine.sol:1559) on the registry's current token, an address this contract does not control.

Permissionless top-up of the bad-debt buffer, with no modifiers at all. It is the only ungated way to raise `insuranceEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1566) directly; the other source is the fee carve at `insuranceEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1366). DERIVED.

The BUY-side native fee credit. The hook selects between this and its sell-side twin by trade direction at `creditPerpFee` (CauldronHook.sol:1203). It deliberately carries no nesting guard because the hook calls it mid-unlock during the engine's own swap; the gate itself lives in the private callee at `hookAddr` (PerpEngine.sol:1611).

The SELL-side native fee credit, selected by the hook at `creditPerpFeeToken` (CauldronHook.sol:1203). Its value lands in the segregated token-staker pot at `tokYieldEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1621) rather than in the PLV.

The ERC20 fee path, reached through the hook's route at `creditPerpFeeAsset` (CauldronHook.sol:1204). It is PULL rather than push - the hook approves and this transfers - because a bare balance could not be told apart from a stray donation. It refuses any asset that is not exactly the current `quote` (PerpEngine.sol:1604) and refuses the zero address. Unlike the native pair it has no side split: both buy and sell fees land in `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1606), which the doc at `creditPerpFeeAssetToken` (PerpEngine.sol:1597) records as a deferred redistribution between staker classes.

Pure accounting, no external call, which is why it is safe to nest inside a swap. It credits `msg.value` (PerpEngine.sol:1617) - NATIVE wei - to either `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1619) or the token-staker pot, and bumps the monotonic marker `tokYieldCumulative` (PerpEngine.sol:1622) that the vault folds into its per-share accumulator. There is no check that the book is currently native-denominated, so under an ERC20 quote these counters would be raised by native value while payouts leave through `_pushQuote` (PerpEngine.sol:213) in the ERC20. DERIVED.

The deposit leg of the community PLV. Called at `fundFromVault` (PerpVault.sol:206) after the vault has already minted shares, forwarding native value only when the quote is native. It has no nesting guard, so it is callable while a sweep holds the lock; it makes no external call beyond the pull. DERIVED.

The only way staked ETH-side principal leaves. It is bounded by FREE capital at `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1642) - lent capital in `longOiEth` (PerpEngine.sol:466) cannot be pulled and returns only as positions settle, which is what the vault's queue exists to absorb. Called from `withdrawPlvTo` (PerpVault.sol:259) and `withdrawPlvTo` (PerpVault.sol:302). The push is the reverting kind, so a recipient that rejects the transfer fails the withdrawal.

Pays an attributed short-side reward out of the segregated pot, never out of `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1646). Reached from `withdrawTokYieldTo` (PerpVault.sol:368). Because the pot is only ever decremented by an attributed claim, yield credited while no token shares existed can never be drained from here. DERIVED.

value: ERC20 `transferFrom` of the generation token from the vault (line 1653)
reachability: The token-side deposit leg, called at `fundTokenFromVault` (PerpVault.sol:357) after the vault has pulled from the depositor and approved this engine. Like the owner-funded twin it does not check the transfer's return value at `transferFrom` (PerpEngine.sol:1653). DERIVED. The pull is a direct `transferFrom` (PerpEngine.sol:1653) on the registry's current token, an address this contract does not control.

value: ERC20 transfer of the generation token to `to` via `_safeTransfer` (line 1661)
reachability: Pays free inventory out, bounded by `plvToken` (PerpEngine.sol:1659); lent inventory returns only as shorts buy back. Called from `withdrawPlvTokenTo` (PerpVault.sol:392) and `withdrawPlvTokenTo` (PerpVault.sol:409). It pays in the registry's CURRENT token, so after a relaunch a queued token claim is settled in the new generation's token. DERIVED.

Fee configuration behind a single owner call. Every field is range-checked at `BadParam` (PerpEngine.sol:1666): the open fee and liquidation penalty cap at 2000 bps, the rest at BPS. Changes are immediate and apply to positions already open, because `liqPenaltyBps` (PerpEngine.sol:1199) and `keeperBps` (PerpEngine.sol:1201) are read at settlement time, not at open. DERIVED.

Risk configuration. Two bounds matter beyond the obvious: the warmup floor at `MIN_TWAP` (PerpEngine.sol:1674) keeps positions from existing while the mark would still be spot, and the funding-rate ceiling at `_fundingBpsDay` (PerpEngine.sol:1691) keeps the signed step arithmetic in `fundingRateBpsPerDay` (PerpEngine.sol:732) inside int256 - an unbounded rate would either invert the funding direction or revert every path that pokes funding. Raising `maintenanceBps` (PerpEngine.sol:1692) makes already-open positions liquidatable immediately. DERIVED.

Replaces both leverage tier arrays wholesale. The only invariant enforced is the length relation at `levs` (PerpEngine.sol:1707), which is exactly what `tierLeverage` (PerpEngine.sol:701) needs to index i+1 safely; the depths themselves are not required to be sorted, and the loop takes the LAST matching tier rather than the largest. DERIVED.

One setter for all four outbound addresses, folded together for size headroom. `markSource` (PerpEngine.sol:1727) is the most consequential: it replaces the tick every mark, funding and liquidation decision is built from, via `_currentTick` (PerpEngine.sol:534). Setting it to zero restores the primary-pool tick, and a source that reverts or returns a malformed answer also degrades to that, so the failure mode is soft. There is no timelock or validation on any of the four. DERIVED.

The three hardening knobs, all range-checked at `BadParam` (PerpEngine.sol:1731): the averaging window between `MIN_TWAP` (PerpEngine.sol:1731) and two hours, and both bps caps at BPS. `twapWindow` (PerpEngine.sol:1732) directly trades manipulation resistance against mark lag, and is read on every `twapWindow` (PerpEngine.sol:638).

Rotates the role that controls the working-capital surface. The drain guard asks the OUTGOING vault whether anyone still owns value, at `hasStakers` (PerpEngine.sol:1752), rather than testing engine balances - so unownable residue cannot latch the guard permanently. Note the call is typed and un-caught, so the incumbent vault can block its own replacement by reverting; and while `vault` (PerpEngine.sol:1752) is zero the guard is skipped entirely.
observations: comment at `PLV` (PerpEngine.sol:1738) says a wired vault may only be re-pointed while the PLV is empty on all three counters; the code at `hasStakers` (PerpEngine.sol:1752) instead asks the vault whether it has stakers, and a later note at `residues` (PerpEngine.sol:1744) explains why the balance test was replaced.

reachability: Sets how much of every routed fee is retained inside the engine instead of leaving to dividend and treasury. The only check is that the pair sums to at most BPS at `_yieldBps` (PerpEngine.sol:1758), so the owner can route 100 percent of fees to LP yield and insurance, or 0 percent. Both are read on every fee at `vaultYieldBps` (PerpEngine.sol:1353). DERIVED.

Utilization ceiling plus the insurance circuit breaker. Both only bite while a vault is wired, because the checks sit inside the `vault` (PerpEngine.sol:792) branch of the open paths. `insuranceFloor` (PerpEngine.sol:1765) has no upper bound, so a large value pauses opens indefinitely; it is also the configured half of the skim protection at `insuranceFloor` (PerpEngine.sol:1787). DERIVED.

The anti-dust floor, capped at one ether at `_minCollateral` (PerpEngine.sol:1769). It is compared against collateral NET of the open fee at `minCollateral` (PerpEngine.sol:786), so the effective minimum deposit is higher than the configured number by the fee. DERIVED.

The only owner path that removes value from the engine, and it can reach only the buffer: `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1774) and `plvToken` (PerpEngine.sol:1774) are untouched. What is protected is the GREATER of the configured floor and a risk minimum scaled to live open interest at `riskMin` (PerpEngine.sol:1786) - which values the short side at SPOT through `_quoteEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1786) while liquidations use the mark. The destination is arbitrary but non-zero at `to` (PerpEngine.sol:1785), and the push is the reverting kind. DERIVED.

Frontend snapshot of one position: mark value, the figure it is compared against (debt for a long, backing for a short, per `debtOrBackingEth` (PerpEngine.sol:1809)), and the same liquidation verdict the engine itself uses at `_underwater` (PerpEngine.sol:1810). Returns all-zero for a closed id at `trader` (PerpEngine.sol:1806).

A bare payable fallback with no accounting. Native value can therefore enter the engine without touching `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:304), `insuranceEth` (PerpEngine.sol:223) or `tokYieldEth` (PerpEngine.sol:311) - which is required, because pool settlement returns native change to the contract during a swap, but it also means a direct send is an unattributed donation that no counter tracks. DERIVED.
